subject: What Redwood retains by default — prompts, requests, responses (deep dive)
messages:
From: Irene Matthews <security@acme-payments.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jason Lee <devops@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: default capture/retention for prompts vs outputs

Hi Soojin,

Quick one as we work through the security questionnaire for our enterprise contract: can you confirm what Redwood stores by default when a customer uses the hosted API? Specifically:

- Do you retain raw prompts (user-provided input) by default?
- Do you retain model outputs (responses) by default?
- Are request/response pairs retained together or only metadata/telemetry?
- What is the default retention TTL, and is that the same across logs, prompts, and outputs?

We need precise language to put into our internal intake doc and to feed back to procurement. If possible, please point to the official doc or provide the exact sentence we can quote.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Matthews
Head of Security, Acme Payments
security@acme-payments.com

Attachment: SOC2_Acceptable_Retention_Table.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Matthews <security@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Jason Lee <devops@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: default capture/retention for prompts vs outputs

Hi Irene — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR up front so you can paste this into the questionnaire: 

"By default Redwood does not persist raw customer prompts or model outputs in long-term storage for hosted API customers. The default telemetry/operational logs retained for 90 days include request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts, routing decision) and non-reversible hashes of prompt identifiers for debugging. Raw prompt and full response payloads are retained only when a customer explicitly enables logging or for specific features (e.g., evals, auditing) under a separate consent/contract clause. Deletion requests for stored artifacts follow the published deletion runbook and are completed within the agreed SLA window in the contract."

Below are more details and clarifications for the items you listed: 

- Raw prompts: not stored by default. We keep ephemeral in-memory buffers during inference; we only persist prompt text when a customer opts into request logging or uses features that require storage (e.g., long-term evaluation, fine-tuning ingestion), or when required for fraud/security investigations under narrow legal/process controls.

- Model outputs: not stored by default. Outputs are streamed and may be buffered transiently, but we do not write full output payloads to long-term storage unless logging is explicitly enabled by the customer.

- Request/response pairing: default telemetry includes metadata that allows correlating requests and responses for debugging (request_id, model_version, latency, status_code). These telemetry records do not contain full prompt or full response text — we store non-reversible prompt hashes and token-level metrics. When logging is enabled, request/response pairs are stored together as one artifact and subject to the customer's chosen retention window.

- Default retention TTL: 90 days for telemetry and operational logs by default in hosted plans. When a customer enables request/response logging, the storage TTL is configurable and can be set by the customer; enterprise contracts frequently specify longer retention or tailored deletion windows. Dedicated and Private deployments honor customer-controlled storage policies and may default to different values (e.g., retention managed by the customer's S3).

- Data residency: by default hosted telemetry is stored in the region selected at signup (we have US and EU regions). When your organization selects EU residency, telemetry and any enabled stored artifacts are kept in EU-backed storage endpoints. 

- Deletion path: customers can submit deletion requests via the Console or the support API. For hosted accounts, deletion of stored artifacts is initiated within 48 hours and completed per the SLA in the contract (usually within 7–30 days depending on the artifact type). We also provide a confirmation receipt and playbook entry (see link below).

I attached a short table (SOC2_Acceptable_Retention_Table.pdf) that maps artifact types to default behavior — hope that helps. Looping in Marissa and Markus for any contract wording we should provide as standard.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Product Security
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: default capture/retention for prompts vs outputs

Thanks — helpful. A couple of follow-ups from the ops side: 

1) When you say "non-reversible prompt hashes" — what hashing algorithm and do you store any salt? We need to ensure hashes cannot be reversed to reconstitute PII for our PCI scope.

2) For deletion requests: can you provide the exact API endpoint or Console steps so we can automate a workflow? Prefer a canonical example we can script.

3) If we enable logging for a single environment (staging) how do we ensure that production traffic remains unlogged? Is that tenant/route-level?

We attached an example deletion request format we've used with other vendors.

Thanks,
Jason Lee
Senior DevOps Engineer, Acme Payments

Attachment: Example_Data_Deletion_Request.txt

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Lee <devops@acme-payments.com>, Irene Matthews <security@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: default capture/retention for prompts vs outputs

Hi Jason — great questions, answered inline below so you can copy/paste into your ops checklist: 

1) Prompt hashing: we apply a salted HMAC-SHA256 to generate prompt fingerprints. Salt is rotated and stored separately in a KMS-backed secrets store; the HMAC key material is not accessible to application engineers and is rotated per our KMS policy. The HMAC produces a non-reversible 256-bit fingerprint — we do not store the raw prompt when logging is not enabled. This approach has been reviewed by our compliance team for PCI/PII risk profiles.

2) Deletion API / Console steps (example):
- Console: Settings > Data & Privacy > Stored Artifacts > Select artifact(s) > Request deletion > confirm.
- API: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deletions with JSON body {"account_id":"<your-account>", "artifact_ids":["<artifact-id>"], "reason":"customer_request"} — response returns a deletion_job_id you can poll at GET /v1/deletions/{deletion_job_id}. (We will provide a signed example in the support ticket.)

3) Logging scope: logging is tenant- and route-aware. You can enable request/response logging per API key or per route. Enabling for staging keys will not enable logging for production keys. We recommend using separate API keys and routing policies to enforce environment separation.

I'll open a support ticket and attach a machine-readable deletion example and the exact policy text we can include in your SOW. See: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/78421. Also linking our retention playbook for legal/ops: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/retention-playbook-v2

If you want contract-level language I recommend this clause we can include verbatim in the SOW: 

"By default, Redwood Inference does not persist raw prompt text or model output payloads for hosted API customers. Operational telemetry (timestamp, model id, token counts, non-reversible prompt fingerprints, routing metadata) is retained for 90 days unless otherwise configured. Customers may enable request/response logging; retention for enabled logs is configurable and governed by the customer’s selected retention policy or applicable contract terms. Deletion requests submitted via Console or API are actioned per the agreed SLA and confirmed by Redwood with a deletion_job_id and completion receipt."

Let me know if you'd like us to drop that exact paragraph into the contract redline — Marissa is on copy to advise on legal phrasing and the standard enterprise variant.

Best,
Soojin
